result.title: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement for Frontier Reasoning Data Synthesis
result.summary: Generating progressively harder reasoning problems requires synthesis procedures that adapt as the task distribution evolves. Existing task-level recursion reuses generated problems as seeds but leaves the construction harness unchanged. We present task-harness co-evolution, a framework for recursive harness self-improvement (RSI) in reasoning-data synthesis. Online self-improvement converts intermediate solver failures into reusable skills during generation. Post-task self-improvement revises skills, prompts, and workflows after each batch, adopting candidates only when they generate harder valid tasks within a bounded cost increase. Model weights and verification criteria remain fixed. Across mathematics, coding, and science, mean solver accuracy decreases from 100.0% to 54.8% over fourteen evolution rounds. Ablations show that combining both update schedules produces harder tasks than fixed-harness recursion or either schedule alone. The resulting data improves downstream SFT and GRPO performance. In particular, a 27B student fine-tuned on 10K synthesized mathematics examples achieves 62.5% mean-16 accuracy on APEX, competitive with selected frontier-model references. These results support adapting the synthesis harness alongside the tasks to generate increasingly challenging data with downstream training value.

AI.brief_summary: 提出任务与构造「harness」协同演化的递归自改进框架，用求解器失败在线生成可复用技能，并在每批之后修正技能、提示与工作流，以生成逐步变难的推理数据；在数学、代码与科学任务上验证了数据难度递增及下游 SFT/GRPO 收益。
AI.relevance_reason: 方法线索是「把失败轨迹转成可复用技能并迭代修正生成流程」，可能可供核查 LVR 中轨迹训练、监督信号与动态计算分配的设计；但该工作只涉及纯文本数据合成与训练，未触及视觉状态或 latent 推理。
